items.title: Exercise 1.7: the entropy linearization prerequisite (partial)

source.anchor: Exercise 1.7 / (1.E.1), printed p.43 / PDF p.55; reused by Corollary 2.1.2, printed p.50 / PDF p.62
source.attribution: Sinho Chewi's exercise; ASTIS-authored restatement and rigorous analytic prerequisite. No copied textbook or solution-manual prose.

items.statement: The exercise asks to deduce Poincare from log-Sobolev by linearization. Its hint obtains the quadratic KL expansion for a centered smooth compact test. This item maps only the compensated-entropy integral limit, generalized to bounded measurable tests and arbitrary finite measures. The actual normalized-law KL adapter and the LSI/energy/test-domain conclusion remain open. The Euclidean/Langevin route must not be confused with the abstract reversible form-domain statement.
assumptions: The source perturbation uses a probability law pi and a zero-mean bounded smooth test. Compact smoothness is sufficient for bounded measurability in the literal hint.

The chapter-2 PI/LSI formulations use compact smooth Euclidean tests with a positive finite inequality constant independent of the test and perturbation parameter. The broader chapter-1 form-domain conclusion needs a separate closure/core argument.

A centered compact test need not be compact. Corollary 2.1.2 uses the broader bounded smooth class with compact gradient support; compact-test LSI cannot be applied to the noncompact square root of a density without a proved extension.

obligations.label: Actual scalar coefficient, quadratic domination, measurability and finite-measure integral limit
Positive unit-mass perturbation and finite canonical KL identification with the zero-mean cancellation
Actual LSI admissibility, energy/Fisher limit and exact constant
Uncentering to compact Euclidean tests; broader form/core closure remains separate

bindings.boundary: Only the compensated analytic prerequisite has local compilation. Other three obligations remain open; no exercise QA admission or complete source theorem certification.

assumption_deltas.source: A smooth compactly supported centered test for the probability law pi in (1.E.1).
assumption_deltas.lean: Any finite measure on any measurable space and an a.e.-strongly-measurable real function with a finite a.e. bound.
assumption_deltas.reason: The compensated integral needs neither centering nor probability normalization. These are required in the later canonical probability-KL adapter, not smuggled into a supposed complete source theorem.

assumption_deltas.source: Small positive epsilon is sufficient for the source linearization.
assumption_deltas.lean: A two-sided punctured-zero real limit with eventual positivity produced from the essential bound.
assumption_deltas.reason: The genuine calculus argument takes place near density value 1; the totalized log/quotient value at parameter zero is not used as differentiability or convergence evidence.
